_comment: CDC scenario KEYS: MySQL CDC over the binlog (ROW format, FULL row images, gtid_mode=ON), each publisher a replica with a server_id of its own; a change to a keyless table names its row by every column. The binlog has no row for what an ON DELETE CASCADE takes and no event for an UPDATE that changes nothing: --cascades unlogged --noops unlogged. An initial load pins its GTID position under a brief global read lock, so no change is both loaded and replayed. Every way a row is identified, over four variants of the publisher (functions/caps_mysqlcdc.py), each in its own collection: mysqlcdc_in (start_from=tail, flattened rows), mysqlcdc_head (start_from=head), mysqlcdc_struct (columns_format=struct, flatten_columns=False), mysqlcdc_map (columns_format=map). STAGES: (1) domains -- create the mysqlcdc domain, install employeescdc, load the xs seed; (2) collections and (3) functions -- registering a stream publisher STARTS it; (4) actions, tagged live -- a 30s pause for the tail streams to attach (a change before that is not theirs to see), one `modify-data --ops Mix --sets 30` pass (inserts, updates -- accounts' moving its key, ledger's by both columns of its key, devices' by its unique index, readings' by every column -- and deletes), then `sentinel-data --key after-changes`; (5) sentinel -- hold until after-changes is in mysqlcdc_in and mysqlcdc_head; (6) actions, tagged check -- scripts/verify_cdc_ops.py checks mysqlcdc_in from the tail and mysqlcdc_head from the head: it replays the binlog, the create-data seed first, so the seed is checked as a snapshot is, one change at a time with its whole before-image and the row it leaves, nothing of audit (each its own lane: one failing does not hide the other); mysqlcdc_struct and mysqlcdc_map run over the same changes, unchecked: their rows nest the values the check reads flat; (7) monitor. Generated by gen_suites.py. Run: `tdd xp one-shot --suite cdc/mysqlcdc_keys --keep`.
